import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.72

by C. Y. Tang

Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ which is not free or cyclic of prime order,
having the property that every proper subgroup of $G$ is free?

Free groups (by the Nielsen–Schreier theorem) and cyclic groups of prime order have the
property that every proper subgroup is free, so they are excluded.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.72»

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators and
finitely many relators, i.e. to the quotient of a free group of finite rank by the normal closure
of a finite set of relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and relators is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- A free group of finite rank is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (n : ℕ) : IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup (Fin n)) := by
  have h : Subgroup.normalClosure ((∅ : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) =
      ⊥ :=
    le_antisymm (Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (by simp)) bot_le
  exact ⟨n, ∅,
    ⟨((QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq h).trans QuotientGroup.quotientBot).symm⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  have : Group.FG (FreeGroup (Fin n)) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range FreeGroup.of, FreeGroup.closure_range_of _, Set.finite_range _⟩
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
    Group.fg_of_surjective (PresentedGroup.mk_surjective _)
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.symm.toMonoidHom) e.symm.surjective

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ which is not free or cyclic of prime order,
having the property that every proper subgroup of $G$ is free?

Here "not free" also excludes the trivial group, which is free of rank $0$. A proper subgroup
is any subgroup $H \neq G$, including the trivial subgroup, and "free" means isomorphic to a
free group of some (possibly zero or infinite) rank. Since `Nat.card` of an infinite group is
$0$, the condition `(Nat.card G).Prime` says exactly that $G$ is finite of prime order.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.72» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧
      ¬ IsFreeGroup G ∧ ¬ (IsCyclic G ∧ (Nat.card G).Prime) ∧
      ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsFreeGroup H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.72»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (¬free ∧ ¬cyclic of prime order; proper subgroups include the trivial one; free of any rank) match the verbatim statement.
modeling_decisions: Finitely presented is modeled with generators indexed by `Fin n` and relators given by a `Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))`, up to `MulEquiv`; this is equivalent to any other finite indexing via `PresentedGroup.equivPresentedGroup`.
'Not free' is `¬ IsFreeGroup G`; since the trivial group is free of rank 0 (basis over the empty type), this excludes the trivial group, matching the decomposition notes.

'Cyclic of prime order' is `IsCyclic G ∧ (Nat.card G).Prime`. `IsCyclic` is mathematically redundant (prime order forces cyclicity) but kept for literal faithfulness. `Nat.card` of an infinite group is 0, which is not prime, so infinite groups are not excluded by this clause.
'Every proper subgroup is free' is `∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsFreeGroup H`, ranging over all subgroups including the trivial one; `IsFreeGroup` allows any rank (zero, finite, or infinite).
The existential quantifies over `G : Type`, following the convention of the other Kourovka files; finitely presented groups are countable, so this loses no generality.

# Conjecture 8.72

by C. Y. Tang

Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ which is not free or cyclic of prime order,
having the property that every proper subgroup of $G$ is free?

Free groups (including the trivial group, which is free of rank $0$) have this property by the
Nielsen–Schreier theorem, and a cyclic group of prime order has the trivial group as its only
proper subgroup. The problem excludes these trivial examples.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.72»

/-- A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$, i.e. to the quotient of the free group on
finitely many generators by the normal closure of finitely many relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))

/-- A group given by finitely many generators and relators is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- Being finitely presented is invariant under group isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H] (e : G ≃* H)
    (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : IsFinitelyPresented H := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨f⟩⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨n, rels, ⟨e.symm.trans f⟩⟩

/--
Does there exist a finitely presented group $G$ which is not free or cyclic of prime order,
having the property that every proper subgroup of $G$ is free?

Here "proper subgroup" means any subgroup $H \neq G$, including the trivial subgroup, and
"free" means isomorphic to a free group of some (possibly zero, possibly infinite) rank.

      ¬ IsFreeGroup G ∧ ¬ (IsCyclic G ∧ (Nat.card G).Prime) ∧
      ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsFreeGroup H := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.72»
